name: Everand
subcategory: music services and creator audio tools
tagline: Organize legally owned ebooks and audiobooks in a private reading library

pricing.notes: Typical monthly subscription; regional pricing may vary.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 1 unlock/month; 1.5 million+ unlock catalog; 20,000+ unlimited-access titles.

tiers.name: Plus
tiers.limits: 3 unlocks/month; 1.5 million+ unlock catalog; 20,000+ unlimited-access titles.

tiers.name: Deluxe
tiers.limits: 5 unlocks/month; 1.5 million+ unlock catalog; 20,000+ unlimited-access titles.
tiers.notes: Official launch material says Deluxe was not available through app-store billing at publication.

pricing.billingTerms: Monthly only; no annual plan was publicly offered. A 30-day trial/1 promotional unlock is not a permanent free tier.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Unused unlocks roll for at most 6 months and then expire; unlocked books remain accessible only while the subscription stays active; Scribd and SlideShare are separate subscriptions.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Everand, organize legally owned ebooks and audiobooks in a private reading library. The hard boundary is licensed book and audiobook catalog, publisher relationships, discovery, and apps, plus licensed content, rights, and distribution network.
coreLoopDIY: Organize legally owned ebooks and audiobooks in a private reading library, index the local files, and provide a private reading and playback workflow.
whatYouLose: licensed book and audiobook catalog, publisher relationships, discovery, and apps
moatNotes: licensed content, rights, and distribution network
ongoingBurden: catalog licensing, royalties, identity, content delivery, moderation, recommendations, payouts, codecs, and rights disputes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Everand because the product is the catalog, rights chain, and distribution network; a player or processing tool is only the visible edge. The recurring cost buys catalog licensing, royalties, identity, content delivery, moderation, recommendations, payouts, codecs, and rights disputes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Navidrome
priorArt.desc: Active open-source personal music server for legally owned libraries.

alternatives.name: Audiobookshelf
alternatives.desc: A private audiobook shelf with a basic ebook reader; it is a library, not a bookstore.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Everand plan and a personal library or creator utility DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Everand in an empty repository.
Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, SQLite, ffmpeg, and a local web interface; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: organize legally owned ebooks and audiobooks in a private reading library, index the local files, and provide a private reading and playback workflow.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Index only user-selected folders and preserve source audio without modification.
Read tags and artwork, calculate loudness and waveform data, and detect exact duplicates by hash.
Provide albums, artists, playlists, search, queue, favorites, and resumable local playback.
Add optional creator tools for trim, normalize, split stems through a local model, and export new files.
Keep all rights and source information attached to imported tracks and display it during export.
Document that the application does not provide music, licensing, distribution, or royalty collection.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out copyrighted catalog acquisition or sharing.
Deliberately leave out streaming-service circumvention.
Deliberately leave out royalty accounting, label distribution, and global content delivery.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
